objective: Development of innovative therapeutic approaches for stress-induced gastritis (neurogenic gastritis caused by stress/psychological factors)
constraints: Must be repeatedly applicable given the chronic nature of the disease
Must be grounded in biological mechanisms
Must be a challenging and innovative strategy beyond existing treatments

objective: Developing a novel research framework to elucidate the pathophysiology of atopic dermatitis (AD) across multiple axes and propose therapeutic strategies based on mechanistic insights
constraints: Must utilize transgenic mouse models or organ-on-a-chip platforms
Must incorporate scRNA-seq-based analysis
Focus on pathophysiological mechanism elucidation
Must address all four pathophysiological domains: skin barrier dysfunction, immune dysregulation, neuro-immune axis, and microbiome interactions
Must propose therapeutic approaches based on identified mechanisms

objective: Development of novel therapeutics targeting the biological mechanisms of allergic rhinitis
constraints: Explore the full spectrum of allergic rhinitis-related mechanisms
No restriction on therapeutic modality; must be a novel approach that overcomes limitations of existing treatments
Clinical goals are symptom relief and prevention
Aim for comprehensive improvement in efficacy, side effects, and dosing convenience

objective: Designing a POC experiment to investigate how sequential and time-differential treatment with S. epidermidis and S. aureus-derived signals (bacterial cocktail or exosomes) affects skin stem cell inflammatory status and differentiation capacity in skin organoids
constraints: Experiment duration within 3 months
Bacterial strains: S. aureus (pathobiont) and S. epidermidis (commensal)
Treatment approach: sequential strain switching with differential exposure duration (e.g., pathobiont long-term then commensal short-term, or reverse)
Treatment format: bacterial cocktail or bacterial-derived exosomes
Plasticity readouts: inflammatory status and differentiation capacity
POC-level experimental scale

objective: Developing a strategy to achieve bidirectional immune tuning through gut serotonin modulation
constraints: Target homeostatic (steady-state) conditions rather than disease states
Focus on gut-derived serotonin (distinct from CNS serotonin)
Utilize pharmacological intervention and genetic engineering approaches
Target intestinal epithelial cells as the primary cellular focus
Consider both autocrine and paracrine signaling effects

objective: Design hPSC-CM-based engineered myocardial tissue for transplantation that electrically integrates with host myocardium and is activated by host excitation, conducting and contracting in synchrony, without functioning as an independent rhythm source.
constraints: Conduction competence and automaticity must be decoupled at the design stage — not by waiting for maturation — to fundamentally prevent engraftment arrhythmia.
Suppression of automaticity must not compromise excitability, conduction velocity, or contractile contribution.
The quiescent, non-arrhythmogenic state must be guaranteed at the tissue level, not merely at the single-cell level.

The host-driven state must hold from the immediate post-graft period (incomplete coupling, inflammatory milieu) through chronic integration, and under catecholaminergic stimulation, ischemic challenge, and electrolyte perturbation.

objective: Develop an experimental framework to demonstrate that skin-resident mast cells exhibit trained immunity-like memory responses upon repeated exposure to endogenous stress hormones (e.g., cortisol, catecholamines, CRH) at specific local sites
constraints: Must use both in vitro mast cell culture systems and in vivo mouse models in parallel
Must establish a readout system for quantitative measurement of secretome composition and relative proportions
Must include separate individual quantification methods for histamine and tryptase apart from the total secretome analysis
Must identify priority downstream target cells affected by mast cell secretome
Must characterize site-specific response patterns following repeated exposure

objective: Develop therapeutic strategies to reduce adipocyte-driven inflammation in obesity by targeting the biological mechanisms through which adipocytes promote inflammation
constraints: Must directly target biological mechanisms by which adipocytes increase inflammation
Must be experimentally validatable
Available experimental platforms: organ-on-a-chip, transgenic mouse model, scRNA-seq

objective: Develop novel anticancer therapeutic strategies targeting epigenetic regulatory mechanisms of autophagy
constraints: Must consider the context-dependent dual role of autophagy in cancer (tumor suppressor in early stages vs. tumor promoter in advanced stages)
Must incorporate key transcription factors (MiT/TFE family, FOXO family, p53) and stress-responsive pathways mediated by mTORC1 and AMPK
Must be experimentally validatable as a therapeutic approach

objective: Developing novel therapeutic strategies targeting the biological mechanisms of diabetic neuropathy in diabetic patients
constraints: Molecular mechanism-centered approach
Available technologies: organ-on-a-chip, transgenic mouse model, scRNA-seq
Exclude Schwann cell-centric approaches; focus on alternative cellular compartments such as DRG neurons, vascular endothelium, immune cells, satellite glial cells, or systemic metabolic targets

objective: Develop a novel therapeutic strategy for obesity-associated psoriasis based on reprogramming immunity mechanisms at the metabolic-epidermal interface
constraints: Mechanism must be grounded in metabolic-epidermal interface and immune reprogramming
No restriction on specific immune cell populations (multiple immune cell targets allowed)
Diverse therapeutic modalities permitted (small molecule, biologics, cell therapy, gene therapy, etc.)
Experimental validation achievable within 3 months
Must be testable using organ-on-a-chip or transgenic mouse models
Balance novelty and scientific challenge with practical feasibility

objective: Develop a Lactobacillus or Bifidobacterium-based hydrogel that enables selective colonization of probiotic bacteria on orthopedic implant surfaces and inhibits S. aureus / S. epidermidis biofilm formation
constraints: Proof-of-concept experimental design achievable within 3 months
Hydrogel-based platform (e.g., alginate, GelMA)
Pathogen controls: S. aureus, S. epidermidis
Probiotic strains: Lactobacillus or Bifidobacterium species
Application context: titanium orthopedic implant surfaces
Must employ novel and differentiated approaches compared to existing research

objective: Develop novel approaches to overcome inflammation and signal quality degradation in chronic neural implants — either by resolving limitations of existing strategies or by employing fundamentally different mechanisms from current paradigms
constraints: Must maintain stable performance over multi-month to multi-year chronic applications
Must resolve long-term stability issues of coatings/hydrogels (swelling, delamination, fragment release)
Must overcome compensatory immune cell responses (astrocyte/macrophage substitution when microglia are depleted)
Must resolve photothermal and phototoxicity safety threshold issues for optogenetic applications
Must consider translatability to large animals and human scale
Must maintain compatibility with neural recording/stimulation functions (electrical or optical)

objective: Development of a novel methodology to effectively deliver protein therapeutics that cannot cross the BBB to specific brain regions
constraints: Non-invasive systemic administration
BBB crossing through molecular biological mechanisms (excluding physical opening or external device dependence)
Target cargo: protein therapeutics
Novel transport mechanism differentiated from existing RMT pathways (TfR, LRP1, etc.)
Capability for specific brain region targeting

objective: Develop a technology for regulating human sleep induction and wake promotion
constraints: Safety assurance (minimize side effects)
Prevention of tolerance development
Repeatability (maintain efficacy with long-term use)
Bidirectional control capability (both sleep induction and wake promotion)

objective: Developing a non-invasive technology for everyday emotion regulation (reducing anxiety and depression) in the general population
constraints: Must be non-invasive
Target general population for everyday emotion regulation, not clinical patients
Must not be a simple application of established single technologies (tDCS, TMS, 40Hz gamma stimulation, temporal interference, etc.)
Must involve novel mechanisms or unexplored combinations of existing elements that have not been sufficiently explored in the literature

objective: Design a novel therapeutic strategy for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) by exploiting TNBC's unique biological characteristics and the physical/physiological/anatomical properties of breast cancer, rather than relying on conventional receptor targets (ER, PR, HER2).
constraints: Exclude approaches based on conventional actionable therapeutic targets (ER, PR, HER2). Instead, leverage molecular and cellular-level intrinsic features (genomic instability, phenotypic plasticity, immune microenvironment, metabolic rewiring, EMT, etc.) as well as physical and anatomical characteristics of breast cancer (superficial body location, structural and physiological properties of mammary tissue, physical properties of the tumor mass, etc.) as the mechanistic basis for the therapeutic strategy.
Ensure tumor selectivity that minimizes toxicity to normal cells.

objective: Develop a strategy to bypass or resolve the selectivity problem between LSC and HSC through a fundamentally different approach rather than molecular target discovery
constraints: Must not rely on conventional molecular target discovery such as new surface markers or signaling molecules
Must reduce or circumvent myelotoxicity (HSC damage), the common bottleneck across current AML therapies
Must be operable under the biological constraint that LSC are direct descendants of HSC, sharing extensive phenotypic and functional overlap

objective: Design a novel therapeutic strategy for brain tumors (especially GBM) that exploits the unique biological characteristics of brain tumors — spanning molecular signatures, organ-level, and organism-level features — as therapeutic leverage points, representing a paradigmatically distinct approach from existing strategies.
constraints: Must overcome general cancer challenges including intratumoral heterogeneity, cell-state plasticity, resistance evolution, and immune evasion
Must simultaneously address brain tumor-specific obstacles: BBB/BTB, infiltrative growth pattern, myeloid-dominant immunosuppressive TME, and constraints on normal brain tissue toxicity

Must exploit unique characteristics of brain tumors not merely as obstacles to overcome but as therapeutic leverage points, considering molecular signatures through organ-level and organism-level features comprehensively
Must be fundamentally distinct from existing approaches such as conventional small molecules, monoclonal antibodies, standard CAR-T, and simple checkpoint inhibitors
Must minimize side effects and maintain or improve patient quality of life

objective: Design a gut-based system that autonomously counteracts hypothalamic hunger-driven weight regain after dieting, operating through a novel signaling modality distinct from canonical satiety peptides and vagal afferent pathways.
constraints: Must operate at the level of the enteric nervous system or enteroendocrine cells, not as a centrally administered agent.
Must explicitly exclude conventional satiety effectors: GLP-1, PYY, CCK, and classical vagal afferent activation pathways.
Must employ a novel or unconventional signaling mechanism to communicate a satiety memory from the gut to central feeding circuits.
Must address or circumvent the problem of central desensitization to peripheral input.
Must generate a signal of sufficient magnitude and durability to counteract established hypothalamic circuit adaptations (AgRP/NPY potentiation, reduced POMC tone, leptin decline).

objective: Design a synthetic anti-obesity homeostatic circuit that automatically normalizes appetite, energy expenditure, and nutrient partitioning when body fat exceeds a healthy set point, thereby correcting the biological asymmetry where weight-gain defense is insufficient compared to the robust weight-loss defense.
constraints: The circuit must sense body fat levels and activate automatically when a defined set point is exceeded.
The output must modulate at least three axes: appetite suppression, energy expenditure increase, and nutrient partitioning away from fat storage.
The design must be mechanistically clear, elegant, and not overly complex.
The approach must be novel and scientifically creative.
The design must be oriented toward clinical translation in humans.

objective: Discover a fundamentally novel "metabolic checkpoint" — a discrete, switch-like molecular gatekeeper that governs the transition from reversible metabolic dysfunction to irreversible metabolic disease — and define a therapeutic strategy to modulate it.
constraints: The concept must be genuinely novel, not a repackaging of established targets (AMPK, mTOR, PPARs, GLP-1R, FGF21, etc.).

The search space must be broad: endogenous metabolic intermediates, microbiome-derived metabolites, inter-organ endocrine signals, epigenetic metabolic switches, immune-metabolic crosstalk nodes, or any other class of biological regulator.

The target must exhibit checkpoint character — a binary or threshold-driven gating function that commits tissue or systemic metabolism toward pathological progression, analogous to how PD-1/PD-L1 engagement commits the immune system to tolerance.
The target must be druggable (small molecule, biologic, engineered microbe, metabolite analog, etc.).
The therapeutic window should focus on disease interception — halting or reversing progression before irreversible damage (fibrosis, beta-cell exhaustion, cardiovascular remodeling).
Tissue-agnostic framing is preferred; the checkpoint may operate across liver, adipose, gut, pancreas, or systemically.

objective: Design a cell-free, implant-free strategy to induce a transient, self-terminating tertiary regenerative niche at a volumetric muscle loss or critical-size bone defect site, capable of autonomously recruiting and spatiotemporally organizing endogenous stem/progenitor cells, immune populations, vasculature, and matrix remodeling through a staged repair program.
constraints: Entirely cell-free — no transplanted or exogenous cells.
No permanent implants or indwelling hardware; all deployed components must be fully resorbable or self-dissolving.
Must recruit endogenous progenitor/stem cells (e.g., satellite cells, MSCs, periosteal progenitors), immune populations, and vascular ingrowth to the defect site.
Must impose spatial organization on recruited populations — not merely chemotactic recruitment, but architectural patterning of the regenerating tissue.
Must execute a temporally staged repair sequence (e.g., controlled inflammation → progenitor expansion → differentiation → matrix remodeling/maturation).
Must incorporate a self-dissolution or termination mechanism intrinsically coupled to a functional readout of tissue restoration (closed-loop feedback, not a pre-set timer).
The niche is tertiary — induced de novo at the injury, not reliant on pre-existing stem cell niches.
Tissue contexts: volumetric muscle loss and/or critical-size bone defects.
Emphasis on mechanistic novelty and creative first-principles design.

objective: Develop a methodology to rapidly and accurately quantify the mixing ratio of exosomes derived from two different cell types in a blended sample.
constraints: Must be able to distinguish exosomes originating from two different cell types
Must provide quantitative measurement across a wide range of mixing ratios (e.g., 20:80, 50:50, 80:20)
Must achieve both high speed and high accuracy in analysis
Must be implementable at lab-scale and ultimately scalable to larger manufacturing processes
Not limited to biological methods; engineering, physical, and interdisciplinary approaches including novel and unconventional strategies are strongly encouraged

objective: Develop an extracellular vesicle (EV) platform whose surface glycans are redesigned exogenously (post-isolation, cell-free glycoengineering) so that the EVs selectively deliver cargo to cells in a damage/inflammation state rather than to a specific cell type.
constraints: Targeting criterion must be the pathological state of the cell (damage/inflammation) rather than cell identity or lineage.
Surface glycan manipulation must be performed exogenously on isolated EVs (cell-free, post-isolation glycoengineering), not through genetic modification of producer cells.
The engineered glycans must recognize receptors or lectins that are specifically expressed or exposed on the surface of damaged/inflamed cells.

objective: Develop a novel glycobiology-based methodology to predict organ-specific metastasis (organotropism) across pan-cancer contexts.
constraints: Must be a glycobiology-based approach
Must be applicable at the pan-cancer level
Must predict organ-specific metastasis destination (organotropism), not just metastasis occurrence
Must be a novel approach that has not been previously attempted
The final form (biomarker panel, device, computational model, etc.) is open to proposal

objective: Designing a novel strategy that exploits the compositional changes of endothelial glycocalyx at injury sites to selectively promote homing and transendothelial migration of endogenous stem cells or exogenously administered cell therapeutics to the damaged tissue.
constraints: The strategy must be grounded in the premise that tissue-specific glycocalyx composition differences (ratios and structural changes of heparan sulfate, hyaluronan, chondroitin sulfate, syndecans, glypicans) are key regulators of cell migration.
The effect must be confined to the injury site and must not disrupt normal glycocalyx barrier function or systemic vascular homeostasis.
The strategy should be disease-agnostic and broadly applicable, not limited to a specific pathological context.
The target of modulation is the promotion of therapeutic cell (endogenous stem cells or exogenously administered cell therapeutics) homing and extravasation specifically at injury sites.

objective: Designing a novel gene therapy strategy for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) that does not directly correct, restore, or re-express the dystrophin gene (including micro-dystrophin), but instead treats the disease pathology through alternative genetic mechanisms — for example, identifying and activating compensatory gene networks that can functionally substitute for dystrophin loss.
constraints: Must NOT target the dystrophin gene itself for correction, restoration, or re-expression (including micro-dystrophin or exon-skipping approaches)
Must be a gene therapy approach (involving genetic material delivery, gene regulation, or genome engineering)
Must be novel and not previously attempted in preclinical or clinical settings for DMD
Should consider broad pathological mechanisms of DMD (membrane instability, calcium dysregulation, fibrosis, inflammation, muscle regeneration failure, etc.)
Must have a realistic path toward clinical translation (feasible delivery, safety profile, scalability)

objective: Develop a novel genetic methodology to quantitatively assess both engraftment success and polyclonal hematopoietic reconstitution diversity following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT)
constraints: Must be a novel approach clearly differentiated from existing methods such as STR chimerism analysis, TCR/BCR repertoire sequencing, and retroviral integration site analysis
The platform itself can be entirely new, but must be principally amenable to clinical translation (considering patient sample accessibility, cost, turnaround time, and regulatory feasibility)
Must simultaneously evaluate both engraftment confirmation and clonal diversity assessment in a single assay framework
Must comprehensively cover all hematopoietic lineages including myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments
Must enable longitudinal tracking of clonal dynamics for up to 1 year post-transplantation

objective: Develop a prediction system that integrates disease-risk SNP genotypes with cellular state information to distinguish individuals who will actually develop disease from those who carry the same risk variants but remain unaffected (incomplete penetrance resolution).
constraints: Must simultaneously capture SNP genotype and cellular state (e.g., epigenomic, transcriptomic) in an integrated measurement or modeling strategy
System complexity must remain moderate — both experimentally and computationally — to be practical
Must be clinically translatable: realistic sample types (e.g., blood), reasonable cost, and interpretable outputs
Must go beyond conventional polygenic risk scores (PRS) and offer a methodologically novel approach
No restriction on specific disease type or data modality; broad methodological novelty is prioritized

objective: Design a physiological strategy that selectively compensates for the homeostatic impairments (neurocognitive, metabolic, immune, and autonomic nervous system) caused by sleep deprivation under time-restricted sleep conditions, thereby inducing a recovery state approximating that of sufficient sleep.
constraints: The strategy must address not a single system but all four axes: neurocognitive, metabolic, immune, and autonomic.
The strategy must be applicable within restricted sleep duration or during wakefulness — not by extending total sleep time.
The ultimate goal is induction of a recovery state approximating sufficient sleep.
The strategy must be physiologically grounded — based on actual homeostatic restoration mechanisms, not simple symptom masking such as pharmacological stimulant administration.

objective: Design a non-invasive method to selectively reduce excessive sympathetic stress responses in the uterus without suppressing systemic sympathetic activity
constraints: No systemic sympatholysis; non-target organ sympathetic function must be preserved
Target organ is the uterus
Non-invasive modality only
Must downregulate only excessive sympathetic activation, not basal sympathetic tone
Novel and original approach
Safe for human use with no adverse effects
Clinically translatable design

objective: Design a novel topical therapeutic strategy that selectively blocks adipocyte dedifferentiation and myofibroblast-like transition specifically within the pathological microenvironment of keloid tissue, while preserving the metabolic and regenerative functions of normal skin adipocytes.
constraints: Therapeutic effect must be selective to the pathological microenvironment of keloid tissue with no or minimal impact on normal skin tissue.
Metabolic and regenerative functions of normal skin adipocytes must be preserved.
The strategy must be in a topical delivery format.
A single administration must achieve sustained therapeutic effect.

The approach must be novel and previously unattempted, not limited to signaling pathways alone but creatively leveraging diverse pathological features of the keloid microenvironment such as mechanical properties like tissue stiffness, metabolic characteristics, immune microenvironment, physical cues, or any other innovative angles.

objective: Develop a preventive skin regeneration strategy that rapidly identifies skin at high risk of post-laser procedural hyperpigmentation (PIH) or abnormal scarring (hypertrophic/keloid) during the early recovery phase, and selectively suppresses excessive melanin accumulation and myofibroblast overactivation while preserving normal wound healing.
constraints: Prediction and identification can occur up to the early recovery phase post-laser procedure, and rapid intervention after identification must be feasible.
Normal wound healing processes (re-epithelialization, appropriate inflammation, ECM remodeling) must be preserved.
Inhibition targets are strictly limited to excessive melanin accumulation and myofibroblast overactivation; intervention must be selective.
The strategy must be preventive in nature—blocking pathology before establishment, not treating established lesions.
Conventional topical approaches such as depigmentation creams are excluded.
The strategy must be clear, elegant, and novel; avoid unnecessarily complex multi-step mechanistic designs.

objective: Develop a skin regeneration strategy that selectively prevents dermal ECM degradation and subcutaneous fat support structure collapse during weight loss, so that body fat is reduced while skin elasticity and contour are maintained.
constraints: Lipolysis itself must not be impaired; selectivity is required to preserve dermal ECM remodeling and structural integrity of subcutaneous fat compartment fibrous septa while fat volume decreases.
Must address both dermal collagen/elastin network weakening and subcutaneous fibrous septa collapse simultaneously.
Mechanistic approach and platform modality are unrestricted (small molecules, biologics, biomaterials, cell therapy, gene delivery, devices, etc. are all permitted).
Must achieve therapeutic effect with minimal treatment sessions (few-session intervention).
Must have realistic clinical translatability (safety, manufacturability, regulatory feasibility).
Must possess sufficient novelty for patentability.

objective: Develop a cell-based drug delivery system that utilizes living immune cells (neutrophils, monocytes, macrophages, T cells) as drug carriers, leveraging their intrinsic homing ability to selectively release payloads at inflamed tissues or tumor microenvironments.
constraints: Drug loading process must not interfere with the immune cells' native migration, homing, and immune functions.
Payload release must occur selectively only in specific tissue environments (inflammatory sites or tumors).
Target immune cells include neutrophils, monocytes, macrophages, and T cells.
Avoid excessive engineering such as heavy genetic modification or complex synthetic biology circuits; prioritize simple and practical approaches.
Must consider clinical applicability including regulatory pathway feasibility, manufacturing scalability, and safety.
Must possess novelty and technical differentiation sufficient for patent protection.

objective: Develop a chronobiology-based drug delivery system for autoimmune diseases that uses circadian rhythm as the primary sensing axis, integrated with secondary biological phases (inflammatory stage, immune activation state, regeneration phase, cell cycle), to release drugs at the optimal timing — particularly preceding the early-morning symptom flare (e.g., morning stiffness in rheumatoid arthritis).
constraints: Target disease is autoimmune disease, especially those exhibiting circadian-dependent symptom exacerbation (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis).

Primary sensing axis is circadian rhythm: the system must synchronize with the diseased tissue's circadian oscillation and achieve pre-emptive drug release before symptom flare (e.g., during the late night preceding early-morning stiffness).
Secondary biological phases — inflammatory stage, immune activation state, regeneration phase, cell cycle — should be integrated to increase release precision.
The system must operate in a lesion-specific manner, minimizing non-specific drug release in healthy tissues.
The system must sense endogenous biological signals from the lesion microenvironment rather than relying on externally programmed timers or clocks.

objective: Design methodologies/approaches to overcome both experimental and analytical technical limitations of in situ cryo-ET, enabling reproducible and reliable in situ structure determination to be democratized for broader adoption.
constraints: An inherent physical information ceiling exists due to Fourier information loss from the missing wedge and low per-image SNR from dose fractionation across the tilt-series; cryo-FIB lamella fabrication throughput and reproducibility, and cryo-CLEM targeting accuracy remain bottlenecks on the data acquisition side.

On the analysis side, tomogram-level correlations violate half-set independence assumptions, anisotropic sampling and spatially varying imaging parameters prevent direct application of SPA gold-standard FSC frameworks, and a tomography-native validation metric to replace them is absent.

On the accessibility side, large-scale GPU/storage resource requirements and non-standardized pipelines fragmented across different software packages create high barriers to entry for smaller laboratories.

objective: Design de novo proteins that function intracellularly to achieve novel therapeutic outcomes beyond simple target binding, focusing on functional modalities distinct from cell surface receptor agonism or antagonism
constraints: The designed protein must produce a defined functional consequence (e.g., pathway rewiring, condensate modulation, selective degradation, organelle rescue), not merely bind a target
The functional modality must be clearly differentiated from extracellular receptor agonism/antagonism

The design must address an intervention point where small molecules, antibodies, and other existing modalities are inadequate, leveraging protein-scale advantages such as large interface recognition, multivalency, or conformational switching
Methodology is open: computational, experimental, or hybrid approaches are acceptable
The proposal must be scientifically feasible and avoid unnecessary overengineering
Designs predicted to cause severe side effects (e.g., broad proteostasis disruption, uncontrolled immune activation) must be excluded

objective: Develop a novel protein degradation or functional inactivation platform that is mechanistically distinct from existing targeted protein degradation (TPD) modalities such as PROTAC, LYTAC, and AUTAC.
constraints: Must be mechanistically distinct from existing TPD modalities (PROTAC, LYTAC, AUTAC, molecular glues, etc.), though molecular format (e.g., chimeric scaffold) may be similar.
Preferably addresses target protein categories that are currently undruggable or poorly served by existing TPD platforms.
Preferred degradation or inactivation route should be a novel pathway, distinct from conventional proteasomal, lysosomal, or autophagic degradation.
Functional inactivation (not limited to physical degradation) is an acceptable outcome.
Must avoid overengineering: the molecular design should be synthetically tractable and practically feasible to construct.
Must be designed with in vivo applicability in mind, avoiding severe side effects, unrealistic dosing concentrations, or poor pharmacological profiles.

objective: Develop a degradation-based therapeutic strategy that clears intracellular pathological protein aggregates (oligomers and higher-order assemblies) in neurodegenerative proteinopathies, including nuclear compartments where canonical macroautophagy is absent or non-functional.
constraints: The target species must be aggregated or oligomeric pathological conformers, not soluble monomeric forms of the protein.
The strategy must exhibit pathological-species selectivity, preserving the physiological pool of the native protein.
The strategy must be operative in the nucleus, where canonical macroautophagy machinery is absent or non-functional.

objective: Develop a de novo strategy to construct a disease-resistant epigenetic state for preventing Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT), broadly covering multiple CMT subtypes and leveraging diverse epigenetic mechanisms rather than being restricted to a single subtype or a single epigenetic pathway.
constraints: The approach must be epigenetic-level intervention, not direct genome sequence editing (e.g., no CRISPR-based sequence correction)
The goal is prevention (pre-symptomatic establishment of a protective epigenetic state), not treatment of existing disease
Must broadly cover multiple CMT subtypes (e.g., CMT1A, CMT1B, CMT2A, CMTX, etc.) rather than being limited to a single subtype
Must leverage multiple epigenetic mechanisms (DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, non-coding RNAs, etc.) rather than a single mechanism
Target cell types are Schwann cells and axons (neurons)

objective: Design a '3D genome editor' molecular tool that selectively disrupts pathologically formed enhancer–promoter (E–P) chromatin loops while preserving normal chromatin contacts and 3D genome topology.
constraints: Must distinguish pathological E–P loops from normal E–P loops with high selectivity
Post-disruption, normal chromatin topology and contacts must remain intact
Primarily consider structural protein manipulation (e.g., cohesin, CTCF, Mediator complex) as the mechanism of action
Epigenetic editing approaches should also be considered as a secondary or complementary mechanism
The approach must be novel — not previously attempted methods or perspectives
Delivery method is unrestricted, but the total number of delivery events must be ≤3
The tool should operate at the level of 3D chromatin structure correction, not permanent DNA sequence mutation

objective: Design a synthetic gene expression switch that reversibly forms or dissolves specific chromatin loops at targeted genomic loci in response to a single external stimulus (light, magnetic field, or ultrasound), enabling on/off control of gene expression. The system should propose a suitable target cell type and demonstrate clear differentiation from existing optogenetic dimerizer-based chromatin looping systems (e.g., dCas9-CIBN/CRY2 or similar). The idea should be mechanistically novel and fresh.
constraints: Must use a single external stimulus modality (light, magnetic field, or ultrasound)
Chromatin loop formation and dissolution must be reversible
Must target specific genomic loci to induce gene expression changes
Must be clearly differentiated from existing optogenetic dimerizer-based systems such as dCas9-CIBN/CRY2 or dCas9-PhyB/PIF fusions
Should propose a biologically appropriate target cell type that best demonstrates the utility of the system
Should be compatible with or leverage CRISPR-based genomic targeting tools

objective: Develop a novel approach to neutralize PYCR1/2 dependency by overcoming existing compensatory resistance mechanisms
constraints: Must target or achieve a context that bypasses compensatory extracellular proline uptake
Must address both isoform compensation and NADH/NADPH cofactor-mediated metabolic compensation simultaneously
Modality and approach are open and unrestricted
Must incorporate the compartmental characteristic that PYCR1/2 are localized in the mitochondria

objective: Develop a non-invasive methodology to restore unaided vision in adult myopic eyes by permanently (or durably) altering corneal refractive power itself, without any wearable corrective devices or invasive refractive surgery. Both corneal curvature remodeling and stromal refractive index modulation (distinct from LIRIC) are within scope.
constraints: No incision, tissue ablation, or intraocular implants; no molds or continuously-worn devices
Exclude pupil constriction or depth-of-focus extension approaches — must correct refractive power itself
Preserve corneal transparency (maintain fibril arrangement), no induced astigmatism or higher-order aberrations, no degradation of low-light vision or contrast sensitivity
Clinically meaningful correction range: at least −3 D

Must be differentiated from existing approaches: ortho-K, low-dose atropine, corneal cross-linking-based refractive correction (PiXL), electromechanical reshaping (EMR), and laser-induced refractive index change (LIRIC)

objective: Develop a novel methodology to control gene expression by directly rewiring three-dimensional chromatin architecture (loops, TAD boundaries, enhancer-promoter contacts) rather than relying on DNA methylation or histone modifications
constraints: Must not rely on DNA methylation or histone modification changes as the primary mechanism of gene regulation
Must minimize dependence on endogenous epigenetic machinery
Must demonstrate a sequential causal chain: 3D structural change → target gene expression change → cellular phenotype change
Target cell types are epithelial cells or neurons

objective: Discover novel therapeutic strategies that simultaneously improve structural progression (e.g., cartilage loss) and pain in knee and/or polyarticular osteoarthritis, with a mechanism-based approach that can pre-specify the causal pathway linking the two effects.
constraints: Exclusion of crowded areas: IL-1 axis targeting, broad MMP inhibition, complete NGF blockade, and pain-only suppression approaches are excluded.
Modality: Intra-articular injection is excluded. Systemic drugs (including repurposing), devices, neuromodulation, and non-pharmacological interventions are all permitted.
Causal pathway specification: The causal pathway from structural change to nociceptive input must be explicitly defined.
Normal tissue homeostasis avoidance: The target must not be involved in essential homeostatic functions of normal tissues, re-evaluated under systemic exposure conditions.
Sensitization normalization: The mechanism must normalize peripheral/central sensitization rather than simply blocking nociception.
Prospective patient selection: It must be possible to prospectively select a responder patient subset via biomarkers or similar means.
Placebo-exceeding effect size: The design must anticipate an effect size exceeding the high placebo response rate typical in OA clinical trials.
Joint specificity narrative: There must be a mechanistic explanation for why a systemically administered intervention shows selective effects in the joint.

objective: Design a strategy for allogeneic HSCT that eradicates leukemia stem cells (LSCs) without non-selective systemic toxicity, achieving relapse rates equal to or lower than myeloablative conditioning (MAC).
constraints: Must include mechanisms that compensate for the loss of anti-leukemia effect caused by reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC/NMA).
Exclude non-selective systemically genotoxic agents (e.g., busulfan, TBI) from the conditioning regimen.
Must achieve LSC-selective targeting while preserving normal HSC engraftment capacity.
Must include a mechanism to overcome LSC sanctuary within the bone marrow niche (addressing physical sequestration and niche-mediated protection).
Must simultaneously counteract multiple immune-evasion mechanisms employed by LSCs (HLA loss, immune checkpoint upregulation, anti-phagocytic signals such as CD47, etc.).
Must enhance anti-leukemia immunity (GVL) without exacerbating graft-versus-host disease (GVHD).

objective: Develop a novel experimental methodology that enables repeated molecular-state measurements (transcriptome-level) of the same individual cells across multiple time points, tracking their response trajectories to defined perturbations.
constraints: Same-cell repeated measurement is essential — population-level time-series reconstructed by destroying different cells at each time point (e.g., pseudotime) is insufficient
Minimum 7 time points at logarithmic intervals covering a 30-minute to 24-hour range
Perturbation (drug, genetic manipulation, etc.) administration at t=0, capturing individual cell response trajectories thereafter
Simultaneous processing of enough cells to enable statistical discussion of inter-cell response heterogeneity
Mechanism-agnostic: non-destructive repeated sampling, intracellular temporal recording with single end-point readout, optical and physical approaches are all permitted

Must be clearly differentiated from existing approaches: computational inference (pseudotime, RNA velocity), metabolic labeling (scEU-seq, sci-fate), lineage barcoding, few-gene reporter live-imaging, Live-seq, NTVE, nanostraw sequential aspiration
